(Kyiv Independent, Al Jazeera, AFP/Reuters)

items.title: A US official said Putin's envoy Kirill Dmitriev held "constructive" talks with US officials in Washington on Monday about ending the Ukraine war and possible US-Russia energy initiatives once it ends.
items.html: A US official said Putin's envoy Kirill Dmitriev held "constructive" talks with US officials in Washington on Monday about ending the Ukraine war and possible US-Russia energy initiatives once it ends. Dmitriev, who also runs Russia's RDIF sovereign wealth fund, came a week after Trump and Zelenskyy met in New York, where Zelenskyy said they discussed a ceasefire on energy targets; Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Putin in Moscow earlier this month. Sources told Reuters he met representatives of the US Treasury and Energy departments. No ceasefire has been announced, and Russian missiles and drones were still striking Kyiv on Tuesday. (Al Arabiya, Reuters, Reuters via Yahoo News)

items.title: A Russian Tu-95 nuclear-capable bomber crashed during a training flight in an uninhabited part of Russia's Amur region early Tuesday, killing six crew members and leaving one hospitalised, Russia's Defence Ministry said.
items.html: A Russian Tu-95 nuclear-capable bomber crashed during a training flight in an uninhabited part of Russia's Amur region early Tuesday, killing six crew members and leaving one hospitalised, Russia's Defence Ministry said. TASS reported the plane carried no munitions; an Aerospace Forces commission was sent to establish the cause, which has not been stated, and Al Jazeera notes that social-media videos of the burning aircraft are unverified. (Al Jazeera, Kyiv Independent)

items.title: Iran's chief negotiator, parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, warned Tuesday that "no infrastructure will remain safe" across the region if Iran's security is not guaranteed, as Foreign Minister Araghchi left New York still awaiting Washington's formal answer on reopening Hormuz.
items.html: Iran's chief negotiator, parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, warned Tuesday that "no infrastructure will remain safe" across the region if Iran's security is not guaranteed, as Foreign Minister Araghchi left New York still awaiting Washington's formal answer on reopening Hormuz. Araghchi told state broadcaster IRIB he expects the official US response through Qatar by the end of Tuesday; Trump rejected the seven-day proposal on Saturday, and US officials say they want a single deal that includes Iran's nuclear programme. No US reply had been reported by mid-afternoon ET. Fighting has subsided in recent weeks, though Iran has kept targeting ships in the strait while the US relies on its blockade and economic pressure. (The Times of Israel, AP, Al Jazeera)

items.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards published an open letter to Americans on Tuesday, five weeks before the US midterm elections, declaring Iran the victor in the war and saying the US government "must be changed."
items.html: Iran's Revolutionary Guards published an open letter to Americans on Tuesday, five weeks before the US midterm elections, declaring Iran the victor in the war and saying the US government "must be changed." The letter, released a day after the war passed seven months, accuses the Trump administration of misleading Americans about the war, Iran's nuclear programme and control of Hormuz while distinguishing the US government from its people. It is a message from one party to the war; Araghchi said Monday that Iran's negotiating position has not changed. (Al Jazeera, Reuters)

items.title: Iranians are stockpiling food and medicine as fears grow of new fighting with the US and of shortages under a tightening US naval blockade and embargo, Al Jazeera reported from Tehran on Tuesday.
items.html: Iranians are stockpiling food and medicine as fears grow of new fighting with the US and of shortages under a tightening US naval blockade and embargo, Al Jazeera reported from Tehran on Tuesday. Shops remain stocked, but social-media posts urge people to hold several days of supplies; the US has also announced a worldwide ban on Iranian airlines and is pressing other countries to cut trade with Iran. Trump rejected Iran's seven-day truce offer on Saturday, and the war is in its eighth month. The rial fell past 2.5 million to the dollar on the Tehran market Tuesday, a new record low, AP reported; rates quoted by different outlets for Monday and earlier this month vary between about 2.2 and 2.44 million. (Al Jazeera, AP)

items.title: Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Tuesday that "we stated our conditions, but Trump is incapable of decision-making" and is "trapped in a quagmire where he can neither negotiate nor fight."
items.html: Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Tuesday that "we stated our conditions, but Trump is incapable of decision-making" and is "trapped in a quagmire where he can neither negotiate nor fight." Rezaei, who heads Iran's Supreme National Security Council, spoke at a meeting with Azerbaijan's deputy prime minister and called the US airline sanctions an "air blockade" and a sign of "desperation"; he did not announce that his window for a US answer had lapsed. Foreign Minister Araghchi said Monday that Iran has not changed its seven-point plan and awaits a formal US reply through Qatar. (CBS News live blog)

items.title: The US Treasury sanctioned 10 individuals and entities on Tuesday for procuring weapons and components for Iran's defence ministry, the latest action under its "Operation Economic Outcast" campaign.
items.html: The US Treasury sanctioned 10 individuals and entities on Tuesday for procuring weapons and components for Iran's defence ministry, the latest action under its "Operation Economic Outcast" campaign. Treasury says the targets, in multiple jurisdictions, supplied the Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics, which oversees Iran's ballistic-missile and drone programmes; Reuters reports they include entities in China, Hong Kong and Pakistan. Secretary Bessent said Treasury "will not tolerate any support to the regime." (US Treasury, Reuters)

items.title: Israel killed Izz al-Din al-Beik, head of Hamas's armed wing in northern Gaza, in an airstrike on a Gaza City apartment building early Tuesday; Hamas confirmed his death.
items.html: Israel killed Izz al-Din al-Beik, head of Hamas's armed wing in northern Gaza, in an airstrike on a Gaza City apartment building early Tuesday; Hamas confirmed his death. Prime Minister Netanyahu and Defence Minister Katz announced the killing jointly on X, and al-Shifa Hospital said a second person later died of wounds. Israel's military says it has killed at least 20 Hamas members this month, including senior commanders; Hamas accuses Israel of undermining the October ceasefire, and Gaza's health ministry counts more than 1,400 Palestinians killed since it took effect. (Al Jazeera, Reuters, The Times of Israel)

items.title: Prime Minister Netanyahu said Tuesday that Israel has "indications" its enemies will try to attack ahead of the elections scheduled for the end of October, and warned: "Don't mess with us."
items.html: Prime Minister Netanyahu said Tuesday that Israel has "indications" its enemies will try to attack ahead of the elections scheduled for the end of October, and warned: "Don't mess with us." He spoke in a video filmed at the Tel Nof air base and gave no details of the intelligence; Israeli forces continue to strike towns in southern Lebanon despite a June deal on a gradual withdrawal, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. (The Times of Israel, CNA, AFP)

items.title: Yemen's UN envoy, Hans Grundberg, said Tuesday he met the Houthis' chief negotiator in Muscat over the weekend to try to head off further escalation, calling the Houthis' attacks on Saudi Arabia "unprecedented" and "dramatic"; the UN counts at least 838 killed and more than 3,640 wounded in the offensive.
items.html: Yemen's UN envoy, Hans Grundberg, said Tuesday he met the Houthis' chief negotiator in Muscat over the weekend to try to head off further escalation, calling the Houthis' attacks on Saudi Arabia "unprecedented" and "dramatic"; the UN counts at least 838 killed and more than 3,640 wounded in the offensive. He also held talks in Riyadh with the government and regional powers. The UN migration agency counts more than 145,000 people displaced inside Yemen and over 3,000 who fled to Djibouti; Grundberg said the war has become entangled with the US-Israeli war on Iran and urged that the conflicts be "disentangled" and addressed one by one. (Naharnet, AP)

items.title: The US military's Africa Command called the growing ties between the Houthis and Somalia's al-Shabaab a "highly concerning, escalatory threat to regional stability," the Financial Times reported.
items.html: The US military's Africa Command called the growing ties between the Houthis and Somalia's al-Shabaab a "highly concerning, escalatory threat to regional stability," the Financial Times reported. Security experts told the paper the Houthis have sold weapons to al-Shabaab and trained hundreds of its fighters in drone and explosive use; the Houthis seized the port of Mokha this month and advanced on the Bab al-Mandab strait, through which about a tenth of global trade passes. (Financial Times, via Horseed Media)

items.title: The World Health Organization said Tuesday that Yemen's health system is at "breaking point" as the Houthi offensive spreads, with nine health facilities damaged, put out of service, closed or attacked in Taiz, Lahj and Hodeidah.
items.html: The World Health Organization said Tuesday that Yemen's health system is at "breaking point" as the Houthi offensive spreads, with nine health facilities damaged, put out of service, closed or attacked in Taiz, Lahj and Hodeidah. WHO's emergency director for the eastern Mediterranean, Annette Heinzelmann, said only about 60% of Yemen's health facilities were fully functional before the escalation and that cholera and malnutrition were already widespread; UN figures count at least 145,000 people displaced this month. (France 24, AFP, Arab News)

items.title: The governor of Ethiopia's Afar region told Al Jazeera on Tuesday that Eritrean forces are taking part in the fighting, control more than two-thirds of Afar and are moving to cut the road linking Djibouti and Eritrea; Eritrea has not responded, and Ethiopia's army says it has killed about 270 Tigrayan fighters and wounded more than 200 in North Wollo.
items.html: The governor of Ethiopia's Afar region told Al Jazeera on Tuesday that Eritrean forces are taking part in the fighting, control more than two-thirds of Afar and are moving to cut the road linking Djibouti and Eritrea; Eritrea has not responded, and Ethiopia's army says it has killed about 270 Tigrayan fighters and wounded more than 200 in North Wollo. The governor's account is a claim by one side that Al Jazeera could not independently verify, and Eritrea and Sudan have denied the army chief's separate accusations of backing the rebel coalition; Egypt said its policy is based on "full respect for the sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity of states." The Afar push threatens the Djibouti corridor that carries most of Ethiopia's imports, including fuel. (Al Jazeera, AP/Reuters)

items.title: Hurricane Polo made a second landfall on mainland Mexico on Tuesday, striking Sonora just east of Guaymas as a Category 1 hurricane with 75 mph winds after crossing the Gulf of California.
items.html: Hurricane Polo made a second landfall on mainland Mexico on Tuesday, striking Sonora just east of Guaymas as a Category 1 hurricane with 75 mph winds after crossing the Gulf of California. It had hit Baja California Sur late Monday with 110 mph winds, and forecasters expect it to weaken as it moves inland with life-threatening winds and flash-flood risk; no casualty reports had been read by mid-afternoon ET. (The New York Times, Reuters)

items.title: Morocco's King Mohammed VI named Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, the 50-year-old mayor of Marrakesh and urban planning minister, as the country's first woman prime minister.
items.html: Morocco's King Mohammed VI named Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, the 50-year-old mayor of Marrakesh and urban planning minister, as the country's first woman prime minister. Her Authenticity and Modernity Party won 97 of 395 seats in the September 23 election, well short of the 198 needed for a majority, so she must build a coalition; she called the appointment "truly historic." (Al Jazeera, AFP)

items.title: Malaysia began sending nearly 1,500 Rohingya refugees back to Myanmar on Tuesday, calling the return voluntary, while the UN refugee agency said it has no role in the operation and that conditions for safe and dignified returns do not exist.
items.html: Malaysia began sending nearly 1,500 Rohingya refugees back to Myanmar on Tuesday, calling the return voluntary, while the UN refugee agency said it has no role in the operation and that conditions for safe and dignified returns do not exist. Dozens of buses under police escort reached a stadium near the Lumut naval base, with two Myanmar naval warships and a hospital ship to carry them; journalists were barred. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said in July that Myanmar had agreed to take back 5,000 Rohingya, and Malaysia hosted more than 126,000 Rohingya refugees as of February. (Al Jazeera, AFP/Reuters)

items.title: The US ban on nearly $1 billion of Canadian imports, mostly alcoholic drinks plus some dairy products and motorcycles, took effect at 12:01am ET Tuesday.
items.html: The US ban on nearly $1 billion of Canadian imports, mostly alcoholic drinks plus some dairy products and motorcycles, took effect at 12:01am ET Tuesday. Trump ordered it to punish Canada for retaliating against the 50% tariffs he imposed this summer on about $20 billion of Canadian goods; the American Action Forum puts the banned trade at $967 million, 87% of it alcohol, and analysts call the direct impact small but say it deepens a standoff that endangers renewal of the US-Mexico-Canada trade pact. Bombardier Recreational Products said its Can-Am three-wheelers will be excluded from the US market. (AP via Yahoo News)

items.title: French civil servants went on strike Tuesday over a planned public-sector pay freeze in the 2027 budget while high-school students blockaded schools, a day after 164 arrests and 180 affected schools, seven months before the presidential election.
items.html: French civil servants went on strike Tuesday over a planned public-sector pay freeze in the 2027 budget while high-school students blockaded schools, a day after 164 arrests and 180 affected schools, seven months before the presidential election. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez gave the Monday figures; Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu called the hard-left France Unbowed party's call to widen the protests "irresponsible" and warned against violence. The CGT union planned more than 150 demonstrations, with the government due to present its 2027 budget within days. (AOL UK, The Local France)

items.title: Myanmar's military killed at least 49 people and wounded 58 in an airstrike near a market in Kyauktaw township, Rakhine state, on Monday, according to the Arakan Army, which holds the area, and a rescue official.
items.html: Myanmar's military killed at least 49 people and wounded 58 in an airstrike near a market in Kyauktaw township, Rakhine state, on Monday, according to the Arakan Army, which holds the area, and a rescue official. The Arakan Army said a fighter jet dropped two bombs near the market around noon, killing vendors, shoppers and pedestrians, and promised "effective retaliatory measures"; AP could not independently confirm details, and the rescue official called the market the region's main wholesale centre. The strike is the latest in a series against resistance forces since the 2021 coup. (The Independent, AP, The Daily Jagran, AP)

items.title: Former special counsel Jack Smith told the Senate Judiciary Committee on Tuesday that his investigation "developed proof beyond a reasonable doubt that President Trump engaged in serious crimes against our nation."
items.html: Former special counsel Jack Smith told the Senate Judiciary Committee on Tuesday that his investigation "developed proof beyond a reasonable doubt that President Trump engaged in serious crimes against our nation." Smith stood by his decision to bring the 2020-election and classified-documents cases and said the firing of career prosecutors and agents who worked on them "makes our country less safe"; Chairman Chuck Grassley called the operation "corrupt" and Republicans pressed him over subpoenas for lawmakers' phone records. The hearing came four weeks before the midterm elections. (NBC News live blog)

items.title: The US Supreme Court on Tuesday let the Trump administration resume deporting migrants to countries other than their own without giving them a chance to raise safety concerns, granting the government's emergency request over the dissent of its three liberal justices.
items.html: The US Supreme Court on Tuesday let the Trump administration resume deporting migrants to countries other than their own without giving them a chance to raise safety concerns, granting the government's emergency request over the dissent of its three liberal justices. The order lifts an appeals-court ruling that the current process breaks federal immigration law; NPR reports the court will also hear full arguments in the case. (Reuters, NBC News)
